subject: Ephemeral/data-retention carveout — follow-up from discovery
messages:
From: Ethan Brooks <ethan.brooks@labspring.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>; Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 31 Oct 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro + data handling overview (LabSpring / Redwood)

Thanks for the call this morning, Rachel and team — good overview. A few clarifications from our side so we can quickly get legal/security aligned: 

1) Core ask: LabSpring cannot persist any full user messages or audio transcripts beyond immediate inference. In practice we need a 0-retention mode for PII-bearing user payloads (we'd accept short-lived KV cache only to support streaming)

2) Logs & telemetry: we can allow request metadata (timestamps, model id, latency) for billing and debugging but need those trimmed to remove user identifiers. Our security team calls this "redacted telemetry".

3) Residency: Production inference must run in us-west or us-east (no EU residency requirement today)

4) Audit evidence: to progress procurement we need SOC 2 Type II report and a short description of where ephemeral mode guarantees are enforced (runtime vs control-plane).

Next steps: can you propose a minimal language for a retention carveout (short bullet points) and confirm technical feasibility (KV-only vs any disk writes) so we can hand to our security/legal?

—Ethan

Subject: Ephemeral/data-retention carveout — follow-up from discovery

Ethan / Sophie — thanks for the time earlier. Short recap and concrete asks so we’re aligned: 

- Summary: LabSpring wants inference with no persistent retention of user messages/transcripts. Telemetry for billing/debugging is OK if user identifiers are removed. Residency limited to US regions.

- What we’ll deliver internally: 1) a proposed carveout clause you can give to legal (one page), 2) a technical note describing where data is kept transiently and what gets persisted, 3) SOC 2 Type II link and evidence pack.

- Quick technical clarifications requested from you (so we can scope the SOW):
  * Does 0-retention need to apply to embeddings and derived artifacts as well?
  * Do you need any request-level debug logs beyond redacted telemetry?

- Proposal for interim compromise (if helpful): Redwood can offer a 72-hour ephemeral window by default and an option for true 0-retention with additional runtime constraints and an attestation. We’ll surface any tradeoffs (no long-running KV cache, feature limits on retry visibility).

Next step: Ethan — can you confirm embeddings and whether your customer success/procurement team prefers a short carveout or full contract exhibit? I’ll loop Aditya/Marissa for technical/security details.

Thanks,
Rachel

Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:37:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Ephemeral/data-retention carveout — follow-up from discovery

Ethan — quick technical note from infra/runtime side: 

- Feasibility: We can operate an inference profile that never writes user prompt/response tokens to durable storage. The model runtime requires an in-memory KV cache to support incremental decoding; that cache can be zeroed immediately after response flush.

- Telemetry: We can emit only anonymized latencies, model choices, and error codes. Any identifier fields are strip-able at the edge.

- Embeddings: if you want to avoid persisting embeddings we can disable embedding caching for your tenant. However, some downstream features (semantic search, reranking) require storing vectors — we can support a separate customer-managed vector store if required.

- Tradeoffs: With strict 0-retention: no long-lived session state, no retries that rely on server-side history, and increased per-request compute which could impact unit cost.

I’ll attach a short technical appendix that we can hand to your security team.

—Aditya

[Attachment: redwood-ephemeral-tech-note.txt]

Subject: Re: Ephemeral/data-retention carveout — follow-up from discovery

Thanks, Rachel / Aditya. A few answers from our side after internal sync: 

- Embeddings: We will not persist embeddings derived from PII-bearing inputs. For non-PII (system prompts, canned text) we can accept short-term storage.

- Audit evidence: please share SOC 2 Type II and a short runtime attestation that ephemeral mode will not log full user messages to disk. We’ll need this before we go to procurement.

- Contract ask: Procurement prefers a one-paragraph carveout in the MSA plus a short SOW appendix that calls out operational constraints (e.g., no server-side session resume).

We’re aiming to get legal review started by Nov 10 if we have the artifacts.

—Sophie
